newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Bomb wounds 13 Ahmadi worshippers in Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: Bomb wounds 13 Ahmadi worshippers in Pakistan.

text.p: A bomb blast wounded at least 13 people of the Ahmadi sect at their place of worship in the town of Rabwah town in Pakistan's central province of Punjab, police said on Tuesday.
They said a time bomb went off on Monday night just before evening prayers, wounding the worshippers, including their local community leader Muhammad Aslam Sabir.
Witnesses said there were 30 people in the congregation when the bomb exploded.

A 1974 constitutional amendment declared Ahmadis outside the pale of Islam, but their leaders say that real persecution began after the late General Muhammad Zia-ul-Haq seized power in a 1977 coup and started a campaign to Islamise Pakistan.
A 1984 decree by Zia banned Ahmadis from using Islamic forms of worship or describing their places of worship as mosques.
The Ahmadis say they have about four million adherents among Pakistan's 130 million people and more than 10 million worldwide.
